CS5-01.note: The colon appositive ('a residue of manufacture with no bearing on how the sheet aged') defines the blank outright: incidental. 'protective' is what the surveys establish AGAINST the old view, so it is the trap for a solver reading the second half only; 'deliberate' and 'corrosive' are unsupported. Nothing eliminable without the passage.

CS5-02.note: 'males recorded forty years apart shared the same terminal trill' pins invariant. The refutation ('drifts steadily and then snaps back') would suit 'stochastic' if the blank described the LATER finding, but the blank sits in the suggested-by-a-single-valley clause. Vocabulary load is the difficulty, not the logic.

CS5-03.note: Appositive again: 'the slow agent of the material's ruin' = corrosive. 'restorative' is the reversed account the cores support, i.e. the trap for reading past the blank. Easy because the gloss is adjacent; the Roman-concrete subject knowledge points the WRONG way (toward restorative), which is a virtue here.

CS5-04.note: 'brevity as a sign that the annotator's engagement was ___' + 'argue otherwise' + cross-references, corrections, a disagreement carried over years = perfunctory. 'sustained' is the state the evidence shows, not the assumption; 'combative' fits only the third clause; 'derivative' is unsupported. See act-mismatch discussion: perfunctory is the only degree-of-effort word in the set, which is a partial blind handle.

CS5-05.note: The last sentence defines the term for you: 'the account that adds fewer unattested entities' = parsimony. Nearest miss is (B) Efficiency, a real synonym of 'economy' in general use, but the text never measures effort or output, only posited entities (two coregencies, a gap in the archive) - so it is a near-miss, not a second defensible reading. 'Prosperity' is the everyday-sense trap, 'Elegance' the aesthetic one. Hard on vocabulary discrimination, which is right for module-2.

CS5-06.note: 'does not register the loss' - the next sentence shows she DOES record the losses (bridge, sheep) in flat syntax, which is what kills (A) Enumerate: under that reading the passage contradicts itself in the following clause. 'Grief enters only four months later' confirms acknowledge. Weak distractors: 'Withstand' and 'Exaggerate' are not senses of 'register' at all and are eliminable on word knowledge alone, so the set is really a two-way contest.

CS5-07.note: 'settled in a way that satisfied nobody' + 'Nothing in the mechanics justified the average' rules out Clarified and Vindicated; the question was closed for a practical reason. (D) Abandoned directly contradicts 'settled' and (C) Vindicated is not a sense of the word - both eliminable without the passage, hence weak.

CS5-08.note: Decided by the last sentence: 'a report nobody outside the field can read is not a report', plus the jargon substitutions and the condescension charge - all about who can read it, none about ornament or candour. (A) Unadorned is the primary dictionary sense and the naive pick, but the passage never touches style or embellishment; (B) Forthright would need a candour cue there is none of. Four genuine senses of 'plain', nothing shape-eliminable. Best-built vocabulary item in the batch.

CS5-09.note: The last sentence names snow-holding directly ('flat surfaces ... hold snow for six more weeks a year'). Options vary in exactly one slot with the frame held constant, so nothing is decidable blind - the clean shape. Easy with the source, which is fine for a function item early in a module.

CS5-10.note: Sentence 2 is the exploitative reading; sentences 3-4 test it against the size of the flat fee and the never-pressed masters. Weak on shape, not on content: (D) is the ONLY compound option ('the fees it paid and the masters it never issued') while A, B, C each name a single comparator - a solver with no passage who plays 'the richest option' lands on it. Fix by making one distractor compound too.

CS5-11.note: passage_needed FALSE: this is the standard mangrove-restoration result (tended monoculture rows survive at high rates while closed stands keep contracting), and (C) is the only option stating it; I could have picked it from field knowledge. Nearest miss is (D) - 'have gone on shrinking' does faintly imply onset before planting - but D does not explain why 80% survival adds no canopy, so it is not defensible as the sentence's function. Weak also on shape: (C) is the lone option with a grammar slip, 'into closed stand' for 'into closed stands', which makes it the odd one out typographically. Fix the article.

CS5-12.note: Sentence 3 is the inference; sentence 4 names guild rolls. Options identical but for the counter-evidence named, none of it inferable blind. Clean, easy.

CS5-13.note: The close is the cost side - biomass to clear, councils funded per cut - so not a favourable comparison (A) and not a dispute of the counts (D). Weak because (B) 'urging councils to adopt the later cut at once' is eliminable on SAT convention alone (informational structure keys do not exhort); it still leaves three, so the damage is limited.

CS5-14.note: Eastern hoards fit, western do not: two regions, one fits. (A) misstates the span, (B) the material, (C) the result. Genuinely parallel, nothing decidable blind.

CS5-15.note: 'only by a fifth of the gap' plus 'The remainder tracks the concentration of a small solute'. (A) and (B) are the two absolutes but they sit as a pair rather than a lone absolute, so neither is a shape giveaway; (D) is a clean quantitative near-miss. Requires holding one number, which is the right kind of medium.

CS5-16.note: The purpose is the last sentence's payoff: readers of the older text agree about the turns because the inversions fall where the Hebrew marks them. Weak on the axis the blind solvers named - A, B and C all explain why the inversions were disliked or removed, (D) alone credits them, and main-purpose keys land on the text's final favourable turn. (C) also imports reading aloud, which the passage never mentions.

CS5-17.note: passage_needed FALSE: park-sited fixed stations versus volunteer sensor transects is THE canonical urban-heat-island siting-bias comparison, and (D) is the only option naming it; I would have picked it from subject knowledge with the source covered. With the source it is near-verbatim from sentence 2. Options are otherwise parallel and none is shape-eliminable.

CS5-18.note: The passage refutes isolation explicitly ('was not isolated; it lay on the main timber road') and offers the wedding rite as the mechanism. Mild axis tell: B, C and D all cite external circumstance (distance, skill, trade) while (A) alone names a functional niche - the shape of the text's own argument. Not enough to decide blind, since three circumstance options survive.

CS5-19.note: Text 2 states the mechanism in its last sentence: a patient awake in the dark and a patient asleep produce the same actigraphy trace, and the check interval rose. A (admission time), C (unblinded scoring) and D (nap counting) are all live measurement objections not raised in Text 2 - the right kind of distractor for a paired-text response item.

CS5-20.note: passage_needed FALSE: 'rotation gain is legume nitrogen, not soil structure' is the textbook agronomy rebuttal, and (B) is the only option naming it. Also the easiest item in the batch with the source - (B) restates Text 2's first clause almost verbatim, so it tests reading location rather than inference. Consider retiring or hardening it for a module-2 hard route.

CS5-21.note: Text 2's objection is a denominator change: once-per-visitor ticketing replaced by per-entry counters in the same year the charge went, with a shared courtyard inflating entries; the household surveys are the corroboration. (C) inverts Text 2's own reliance on surveys and (B)/(D) invent facts - none eliminable without reading Text 2, so plausible rather than weak.

CS5-22.note: Agreement item: Text 1 asserts the shortfall, Text 2 accepts it and re-explains it ('Submission counts fall wherever the odds ... are visibly worse'). (C) is Text 2 only - the standard and correct trap for this item type - and (B)/(D) are unsupported by either. Well built.

CS5-23.note: Text 2's last sentence splits the two outcomes: matched time equalises RECALL (so the recall gap was time on task, not motor rehearsal) but not REPRODUCTION (so motor rehearsal survives there). (A) is incoherent - if time differs, time explains the recall gap, not motor rehearsal; (D) is refuted by the second clause. Hardest reasoning in the batch and the option set is genuinely parallel. But passage_needed FALSE: 'handwriting aids production more than recognition' is the standard finding in that literature, so (B) is reachable from field knowledge alone.

CS5-24.note: Text 2 names the variable directly ('Willow height in the valley tracks the water table') and supplies the controlled comparison (low aquifer, recolonised beaver ponds, no extra growth), which also kills (A). Nearest miss is (D), since the wet winters cause the water table - but Text 2 says willows track the table, not snowpack, so D is one causal step off, not defensible. passage_needed FALSE: the hydrology-not-trophic-cascade objection to the Yellowstone wolf-willow story is the well-known published critique, so (C) is pickable from subject knowledge.

act_mismatch_agree.detail: CS5-06 AGREE: 'Withstand' and 'Exaggerate' are not senses of 'register' in any register, so the set collapses to Enumerate vs Acknowledge before the passage is opened - half the option set is dead weight. CS5-16 AGREE and it is the clearest case: A, B and C all perform one act (explaining why the inversions were faulted, smoothed, or are harder) and only D credits them with a benefit; main-purpose keys land on the text's final favourable turn, so the lone positive is identifiable on the axis alone. CS5-04 PARTIAL: 'perfunctory' is the only degree-of-effort word among a type word (derivative), a stance word (combative) and a duration word (sustained), so a solver who assumes the standard assumption-then-refutation frame has a handle; but the direction of the frame is not recoverable from the options, so it is a narrowing, not a decision. CS5-08 DISAGREE: from the with-source seat this is the strongest vocabulary item here. All four are live senses or associations of 'plain', and the naive blind pick is (A) Unadorned, the primary sense - the key is the third option and requires the last sentence. If blind solvers converged here they converged on the wrong letter, which is the opposite of a leak.

knowledge_key_agree.detail: AGREE on 11, 17 and 23, and I marked all three passage_needed:false independently before reading the flag. Each key is the standard claim in its field stated in the only option that states it - tended seedling rows survive without closing canopy; park-sited fixed stations underread street heat against volunteer transects; handwriting's advantage is in production, not recognition. The option sets are well built and parallel, which is exactly why the leak is invisible to a structural check: the discriminator is domain truth, not shape. DISAGREE on CS5-10. Its key is not a field claim at all - it is a summary of what the following two sentences do, and the revisionist reading of 1920s flat-fee contracts is not standard enough to guess. Its real tell is structural and different in kind: (D) is the only compound comparator in the set, so 'pick the richest option' finds it. That is a shape defect, and unlike the knowledge family it is cheap to fix - make one distractor compound. Worth separating in the ledger so the fix for 10 is not filed under the fix for 11/17/23.

nearest_misses_not_counted_as_second_def: CS5-05 (B) Efficiency - a real synonym of 'economy', but the closing sentence measures posited entities, not effort
CS5-11 (D) - 'have gone on shrinking' faintly implies onset before planting, but D does not explain why high survival adds no canopy
CS5-24 (D) - snowpack causes the water table, but Text 2 says willows track the table
